chunks: A group of our shaykhs said to me, from Abū al-Ḥusayn Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Asadī; and there came to him, among what came of the answers to his questions, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān al-ʿAmrī, may Allah have mercy on him.

As for what you asked about regarding salat (prayer) at the rising of the sun and at its setting: if it is as people say, that the sun rises between the two horns of al-Shayṭān and sets between the two horns of al-Shayṭān, then the nose of al-Shayṭān is not humbled by anything better than salat (prayer). So perform it, and humble the nose of al-Shayṭān.
And that which indicates this detail that we have mentioned.

key_terms.أُرْغِمَ أَنْفُ الشَّيْطَانِ: the humbling of al-Shayṭān, used here for his disgrace and subjugation
key_terms.التَّفْصِيلِ: the detailed distinction or explanation being referred to at the close
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the act being asked about at sunrise and sunset
key_terms.طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ: the rising of the sun, one of the specific times under discussion
key_terms.غُرُوبِهَا: its setting, the other time under discussion
key_terms.فَصَلِّهَا: so perform it, an instruction to carry out the salat (prayer)
key_terms.قَرْنَيِ الشَّيْطَانِ: the two horns of al-Shayṭān, as mentioned in the reported popular saying

ai.seo_question: Can salat (prayer) be performed at sunrise and sunset in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling of performing salat (prayer) at sunrise and sunset, indicating that such prayer is not to be abandoned on account of a popular claim about al-Shayṭān’s association with those times. Rather, the text presents salat (prayer) itself as the best means of humiliating al-Shayṭān, thus supporting the permissibility of performing it in that context.
